evidence: Suet. Jul. 31: quod sī ponticulum trānsierimus
terms.comment: The diminutive of pōns: any small bridge, often of wood, such as one crosses on foot over a ditch or a stream. For a bridge that carries walkers over a road, pōns will do.

phrases.latin: Manum mihi dā, dum ponticulum trānsīmus.
phrases.english: Give me your hand while we cross the little bridge.

phrases.latin: cum fossam lātam cubiculārī lectō circumdedisset ejusque fossae trānsitum ponticulō ligneō conjūnxisset
phrases.english: when he had dug a wide ditch round his bed and joined the way across it with a little wooden bridge

phrases.latin: quod sī ponticulum trānsierimus, omnia armīs agenda erunt
phrases.english: but once we cross that little bridge, everything will have to be settled by arms

phrases.latin: sum enim ipse mēnsus ab eō ponticulō quī est ad Furīnae, Satricum versus
phrases.english: for I measured it myself from the little bridge by Furina’s shrine, in the direction of Satricum
